features.title: Invite codes can't be brute-forced across accounts
checks: Every failed redeemInvite adds a row to a new RedeemFailure table (userId, at; indexed on at; userId references User with onDelete: Cascade), made by a committed migration (npx prisma migrate dev --name redeem-failures).
A refusal while locked, whether by the global limit or the per-account one, adds no RedeemFailure row, so a locked account can't keep the global count up.

Once there are more than GLOBAL_REDEEM_FAILURES_PER_HOUR (30, a constant in src/server/invites.ts) failures in the last hour across all accounts, every redeem returns code LOCKED with 'Too many tries right now. Try again in an hour, or ask Vienne to check the code.', a correct code included.
Vienne gets one alert when the limit is first reached in an hour, sent after the transaction commits (lib/notify.ts), never one per try.
The per-account limit (MAX_FAILURES, LOCK_MS) and the MM-XXXX code shape stay as they are; the w2 spec checks the shape.

hints: Why: 32^4 ≈ 1.05M codes, free accounts and a per-account lock only, so 1,000 accounts could try 3M+ codes in a code's 14 days (VALID_DAYS).

features.title: Redeem limits hold under parallel tries; old failure rows are cleaned up

A right code is checked against GLOBAL_REDEEM_FAILURES_PER_HOUR under the same advisory lock before it's claimed. Past the limit it gets the same LOCKED message as a wrong code, until the hour passes, as S5 says (every redeem returns LOCKED). The code isn't used up.
cleanUp in src/lib/jobs.ts (the daily job) deletes RedeemFailure rows older than a day and returns how many (redeemFailures). Rows from the last hour still count toward the limit.
